policies.summary: Wind and solar facilities of 100 MW or more (and expansions of 25 MW or more that bring a facility to 100 MW) need a Public Utilities Commission permit; the Commission does not choose or mandate locations, and county and municipal zoning still applies, while smaller projects are left to local governments alone.

Each tower of a large wind energy system (tower 75 feet or taller) must be set back at least 500 feet or 1.1 times tower height, whichever is greater, from any surrounding property line, unless the adjacent landowner agrees in writing to a closer placement.

restrictions.description: More than 450 citizens petitioned for a moratorium after the Planning and Zoning Commission approved conditional-use permits (2024-10-28) for the Cheyenne River Ranch Wind and Solar Farm near New Underwood. Active as of 2026-09-23. Pennington County's temporary zoning moratorium on utility-scale wind and solar development (enacted unanimously November 19, 2024, effective December 12, 2024, after 450+ citizens petitioned against the Cheyenne River Ranch Wind and Solar Farm's conditional-use permits) was extended unanimously by the Board of Commissioners on October 21, 2025 through November 18, 2026, to give an alternative-energy task force (formed March 2025) and the Planning Commission time to finish a consolidated ordinance amending zoning Section 3-17. A related but legally separate zoning-ordinance amendment permanently barring utility-scale wind and solar from agricultural (non-industrial) land passed its second and final reading 3-2 on August 18, 2026, after a multi-month back-and-forth (first reading May 19, 2026; delayed multiple times); commissioners indicated the moratorium could be lifted early once the Planning Commission's consolidated ordinance is finalized. Legal basis: Pennington County Board of Commissioners temporary zoning moratorium on utility-scale wind and solar development, adopted unanimously November 19, 2024 (effective December 12, 2024); extended unanimously October 21, 2025 through November 18, 2026, while an alternative-energy task force and the Planning Commission draft amendments to zoning ordinance Section 3-17 (renewable energy systems).

Proposed Swan Lake Wind Project (NextEra Energy Resources; up to 97 GE turbines, approximately 248 MW) spanning Turner and Yankton counties; county sought time to study and regulate before the project could proceed. Extended as of 2026-09-23; the one-year moratorium on new permits and land-use approvals for utility-scale solar and wind systems (Ordinance #100-25, adopted 2025-08-26) was extended one year by Ordinance #105-26, adopted 2026-08-25 after an 8:35 a.m. public hearing (4 ayes, chairman abstaining), and now expires 2027-08-25. NextEra withdrew its Swan Lake Wind application in August 2026. Legal basis: Ordinance #100-25, 'A Temporary Zoning Ordinance Regulating Utility-Scale Alternative Energy in All Turner County Zoning Districts' (adopted 2025-08-26); extended by Ordinance #105-26, 'A Temporary Zoning Ordinance Extending the Moratorium Regulating Utility-Scale Alternative Energy Systems in All Turner County Zoning Districts' (adopted 2026-08-25); SDCL 11-2-10, 7-18A-8.
